'''''Holmskioldia''''' is a genus of [[flowering plant]]s in the mint family, [[Lamiaceae]]. It is native to the [[Himalayas]] ([[India]], [[Pakistan]], [[Nepal]], [[Bhutan]], [[Bangladesh]], [[Myanmar]]) but widely cultivated as an ornamental and naturalized in many places ([[Southeast Asia]], [[New Caledonia]], [[Hawaii]], [[Mexico]], [[West Indies]], [[Venezuela]], etc.) It contains only one known species, '''''Holmskioldia sanguinea''''', commonly called the '''Chinese hat plant''', '''cup-and-saucer-plant''' or '''mandarin's hat.'''<ref name=y>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=99652 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]{{Dead link|date=August 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>Fernandes, R. & Diniz, M.A. (2005). Avicenniaceae, Nesogenaceae, Verbenaceae and Lamiaceae (subfams, Viticoideae and Ajugoideae). Flora Zambesiaca 8(7): 1-161. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref><ref>Nelson Sutherland, C.H. (2008). Catálogo de las plantes vasculares de Honduras. Espermatofitas: 1-1576. SERNA/Guaymuras, Tegucigalpa, Honduras.</ref><ref>Hokche, O., Berry, P.E. & Huber, O. (eds.) (2008). Nuevo Catálogo de la Flora Vascular de Venezuela: 1-859. Fundación Instituto Botánico de Venezuela.</ref><ref>Davidse, G. & al. (eds.) (2012). Flora Mesoamericana 4(2): 1-533. Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, México, D.F.</ref>

The genus name commemorates [[Johan Theodor Holmskiold]] (1731–1793), a [[Denmark|Danish]] botanist who wrote {{lang|la|Beata ruris otia fungis Danicis}}, published in two volumes in 1790 and 1799.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.usc.edu/libraries/archives/arc/findingaids/hancockcollection/rbbooksh/holmskt1.htm | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070506101045/http://www.usc.edu/libraries/archives/arc/findingaids/hancockcollection/rbbooksh/holmskt1.htm | archive-date=2007-05-06 | title=Holmskiold, Theodor. Beata ruris otia fungis Danicis (Copenhagen, 1790-1799) }}</ref>

==Species formerly included==
The following species have been moved to genus ''[[Karomia]]'':<ref name=tpl>{{cite web|title=Holmskioldia|url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/search?q=holmskioldia|work=The Plant List (2013). Version 1.1|access-date=16 March 2014}}</ref> 
* ''[[Holmskioldia gigas]]'' <small>Faden</small> = ''[[Karomia gigas]]'' <small>(Faden) Verdc.</small>
* ''[[Holmskioldia speciosa]]'' <small>Hutch. & [[Amy Corbishley|Corbishley]]</small> = ''[[Karomia speciosa]]'' <small>(Hutch. & Corbishley) R.Fern.</small> – Southern Chinese hats, wild parasol flower 
* ''[[Holmskioldia tettensis]]'' <small>(Klotzsch) Vatke</small> = ''[[Karomia tettensis]]'' <small>(Klotzsch) R.Fern.</small> – Cups-and-saucers, wild parasol flower

The plant contains [[oroxindin]], a type of [[polyphenolic]] compound.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=15532983 |title=Phytotoxic and antimicrobial constituents of ''Bacopa monnieri'' and ''Holmskioldia sanguinea'' |access-date=2014-08-25 |archive-date=2014-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826161111/http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=15532983 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
